name: K-V1
description: The in-game cloud viewer (src/Atmospheres/Viewer): does it work in the running game? One start on the pad with the own cloud pass drawing (Medium, 1707x960, raytracing off, frame generation off, EVE removed). ViewerProbe drives the viewer through the calls of its window's controls (no mouse clicks) and reads the effects back where the game shows them: a. the window opens and closes with Toggle and holds the registry's keys; b. the A/B flip changes the effective values and the own pass's frame reads them back (exposure), and the read check sees the pass read the key; c. the ground pose, the altitude slider and a typed height put the vessel where they say and keep the camera's aim; d. the cloud speed (cloud.motionScale) scales the pass's noise clock and the layers' drift, 0 freezes them; e. the time offset, freeze and resume against the game's clock and the sun, and the forced weathers (Overcast, Fair, Cumulus Field, Rain Deck) against the pass's own map readers, the layer cover at the vessel and the forced precipitation; f. the capture writes the picture and its sidecar with the window hidden through the frame it is read in. Then the window is closed and everything has to be back. Every check logs 'viewer: <what>: expected ..., read ... - ok|FAILED' and the probe fails itself. Cannot be shown without a person: how the window looks and whether its controls answer the mouse (one screenshot of the open window is saved to series-pictures), the hotkey (no default binding), the look of the weathers and of the picture. At most 10 minutes of scenario; the start ends on the verdict, not on a timer. Rows: tests/series/rows/VPROBE.json.

starts.description: The cloud viewer on the pad at 1707x960 (ViewerProbe, module order 992): window, A/B, altitude, cloud speed, time, forced weather, capture, close and restore. About 3 minutes after the flight is up.
